payout_quote: Election Judges can earn a minimum of $250. To receive compensation, individuals must attend training and stay for the entire Election Day (5:00 a.m. to approximately 8:00 p.m.).
steps: Complete the Election Judge Application for the St. Louis County Board of Elections (contact Judges Department at 314-615-1865 or eworker@stlouiscountymo.gov with questions).
Report for duty at 5:00 A.M. on Election Day.

Work the entire Election Day (5:00 A.M. to approximately 8:00 P.M.), performing sample duties such as setting up voting equipment, checking in voters on the Poll Pad, and breaking down/packing up equipment.
catches: Compensation is stated as a minimum ($250); the county does not publish role-based tiers on this page.
Pay requires both training attendance and staying the entire Election Day.
An old 2016 EAC flyer shows $125–$155 plus $30–$65 training, but it is a 10-year-old historical document; the county's current program page supersedes it with the $250 minimum.
biggest_catch: Minimum $250 requires attending training and staying for the full 5:00 A.M.–approx. 8:00 P.M. Election Day — a roughly 15-hour day.
eligibility: U.S. citizen; at least 18; registered voter in Missouri; declare party affiliation (Democrat or Republican per RSMo 115.081); attend training; transportation to and from polling place; working email and phone; not related to a candidate on the ballot; able to lift up to 30 lbs.
timing: 5:00 A.M. to approximately 8:00 P.M. on Election Day.

notes: St. Louis County, Missouri election judges. Minimum $250 compensation requires attending training and working the entire Election Day (5:00 A.M.–approx. 8:00 P.M.). The City of St. Louis's separate $225 figure (stlouis-mo.gov) is a different jurisdiction and is not used here.
